title: Necklace

altText: A gold necklace made of linked gold elements, laid out against a plain background. Its pieces have fine twisted-wire decoration.

context: A gold necklace made in Spain in the 14th or 15th century and held in the Met's Islamic Art collection. The Met notes that its pyramid-shaped and trumpet-shaped elements have designs made only in paired twisted wire, highlighted with pierced areas. It is about 22 centimeters wide and weighs about 18 grams.

descriptions.k: This is a necklace made of gold. It was made in Spain a very long time ago. It has little pieces shaped like pyramids and trumpets. They are decorated with tiny twisted wires. Can you find a twist?
descriptions.g12: This gold necklace was made in Spain over 500 years ago. It has pieces shaped like little pyramids and trumpets. The patterns are made from thin gold wires twisted together in pairs. Some parts have tiny holes cut through them. How do the patterns make the gold look lacy?
descriptions.g35: This necklace was made in Spain in the 1300s or 1400s. It is made only of gold, and it is about 22 centimeters wide but weighs only about 18 grams. The Met says it has pyramid-shaped and trumpet-shaped parts, with patterns made from pairs of twisted wire and decorated with pierced areas, which are small cutouts. How do the twists and cutouts add detail to the gold?
descriptions.g68: This Spanish necklace of the 14th or 15th century shows how much a goldsmith could do with very little material. At about 22 centimeters wide it weighs only about 18 grams, yet it is covered with decoration: pyramid and trumpet shaped elements with designs formed only from paired twisted wire, highlighted by pierced openings. Light passes through the openings and plays across the wire. How does the maker create richness through pattern rather than weight?
descriptions.g910: The Met places this gold necklace in its Islamic Art collection and records that it was made in Spain in the 14th or 15th century. Its pyramid and trumpet shaped elements are decorated solely with paired twisted wire and pierced areas, so pattern is built from line and openings rather than gems or enamel. At 18 grams, it is light for its width. Consider how such restrained means can produce complexity, and how the necklace may have been worn.
descriptions.g1112: This necklace, made in Spain in the 14th or 15th century and held in the Met's Islamic Art collection, exemplifies a jeweler's art built on technique rather than additive materials: forms ornamented solely by paired twisted wire and pierced areas. Such work belongs to a wider Mediterranean tradition of goldsmithing, though who made or wore this piece is not documented. The object invites us to think about how craft traditions cross cultural boundaries, and how museum categories shape what we expect to see.

teacherNote.context: A gold necklace made in Spain in the 14th or 15th century and held in the Met's Islamic Art collection. According to the Met, its pyramid-shaped and trumpet-shaped elements are decorated only with paired twisted wire and pierced areas.
directions: Have students twist two pieces of thin wire or yarn together and draw a pattern from it.
Discuss how an object can belong to more than one culture's history.
Compare this necklace with the Indian gold pendant in the archive and discuss how different jewelers use gold.
